title: Emergency backfill: 12hr hire slate and 30-day onramp playbook
summary: Procedural checklist and templates for sourcing, interviewing, approving, and onboarding a 12-hour emergency backfill candidate plus a pragmatic 30-day onramp for temporary or permanent replacements.
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a repeatable, lean protocol for emergency backfills where a role must be filled with minimal lead time (target: first qualified slate within 12 hours). It covers decision gates, quick sourcing channels, an abbreviated interview rubric, hiring approvals, communication templates, and a focused 30-day onramp checklist to minimize operational risk.

When to use:
- Unplanned absence for >5 business days with immediate operational impact
- Critical customer-facing oncall gap or launch-day failure
- Key role loss during an active release or incident response where capacity is required

Decision gate (People Ops + Hiring Manager):
1) Confirm business impact and duration estimate (hiring manager)
2) Decide backfill type: temporary contractor (preferred) vs fast-perm hire
3) Set SLA: 12-hour first slate (internal+agency), 48-hour offer target
4) Authorize spend cap (hourly/day for contractors or offer band for perm)

Quick-channel sourcing matrix (first 12 hours):
- Internal bench pool (Slack #bench-availability): immediate outreach template below
- Priority agencies (pre-approved emergency vendors) — call + email concurrently
- Alumni/returnship list (internal spreadsheet maintained by People Ops)
- LinkedIn InMail blitz by hiring manager + recruiter (short message template below)
- Cross-team secondments: approach product/eng leads for temporary detailers

Sourcing workflow (parallelized):
- Hour 0: Hiring manager declares emergency in Slack, tags People Ops, staffing lead, and team lead. People Ops opens an emergency req in ATS and assigns a recruiter.
- Hour 1: Recruiter runs internal bench and sends 6 internal reachouts; posts a 3-line emergency job card in #bench and #hiring; pings two pre-approved agencies.
- Hour 3–6: Agencies send candidate lists; recruiter phone-screens promising profiles; hiring manager does 20-min screening slots in calendar.
- Hour 8–12: First interview batch completed; shortlist of 1–3 for fast-offer or contractor engagement.

Abbreviated interview rubric (use for 20–40 minute screens):
Scoring: 1–4 (1 = not demonstrated, 4 = exceeds expectations). Quick rubric categories:
- Role signal (domain experience + relevant tools) — score 1–4
- Problem decomposition (can break work into actionable steps) — score 1–4
- Reliability & communication (SLAs, remote work, status cadence) — score 1–4
- Ramp velocity (past quick-onboard examples, learning curve evidence) — score 1–4
- Risk signals (availability, notice period, conflicts) — score 1–4
Pass threshold: average >= 3.0 and no category with a 1.
Decision rules:
- If candidate averages >=3.5 -> Hiring manager approval via DM (okay to extend offer or contractor SOW).
- If 3.0–3.4 -> Additional 30-min functional check with team lead.
- If <3.0 -> decline and continue slate.

Fast approvals and compensation guidance:
- People Ops keeps a pre-signed emergency spend authorization for up to $X/hr (configurable per role band).
- For contractors: use pre-approved SOW template, limit to 90 days without exec signoff.
- For perm: Hiring manager + People Ops must sign off; Director level approval required for offers above band midpoint.

Communication templates (copy/paste):
Slack emergency post (hour 0):
"ALERT: Immediate backfill needed for [ROLE] on [TEAM]. Duration unknown; impact = [brief impact]. @people-ops @recruiting please stand up emergency req. Need internal/contractor candidate slate within 12h. Contact: [Hiring manager name + calendar link]."

Email to agency (hour 1):
Subject: URGENT: Immediate [Role] for Redwood Inference — 12hr slate requested
Body: Hi [agency rep],
We need 3–5 qualified candidates for [ROLE] (contract, remote/on-site) by EOD today. Must have [top 2 must-have skills]. Fast screen + resume only — hiring manager will do 20-min phone screens. Budget cap: [X/hr]. Can you confirm availability and ETA?

LinkedIn InMail short template: "Hi [Name], urgent short-term opening at Redwood Inference for [role]. 20-min screen today? Immediate start needed. Reply if available — [hiring manager name]."

Offer and SOW templates: store canonical templates in linked_artifacts (see top). Use expedited background check waiver for contractors if allowed by security policy.

30-day Onramp checklist (owner in parentheses):
Days 0–1:
- Access & provisioning (IT) — corp laptop, VPN, account provisioning (IT ticket #)
- Short triage doc from hiring manager: "Top 5 priorities for first 30 days" (Hiring manager)
- Buddy assigned and 3-day shadow schedule (Team lead)

Days 2–7:
- Context handoff: runbook, recent incidents, runbook walkthrough (Team lead + Buddy)
- Quick wins list assigned (3 traction tasks) and 1 PR/patch goal (Hiring manager)
- Daily 15m stand-up for first week for visibility (Team)

Days 8–30:
- Weekly 1:1s (Hiring manager) and 30-day checkpoint meeting (People Ops + Hiring manager)
- Knowledge transfer sessions recorded (Buddy)
- For perm candidates: performance rubric review at day 30 and decision to extend/convert (People Ops + Hiring manager)

Risk mitigation and fallbacks:
- If no slate within 12 hours: escalate to Director of Eng for cross-team temporary detail or pull from Dedicated vendor pool.
- If background/security delays: approve limited-access SRE sandbox token for immediate non-privileged work until clearance complete.
- If candidate declines offer: immediate second-choice offer or contractor engagement.

Operational notes and metrics to capture (postmortem):
- Time-to-first-slate, time-to-offer, time-to-start
- Number of outreach channels used and conversion rates
- Cost incurred vs budget cap
- Feedback from hiring manager on quality of slate

Maintenance and ownership:
- People Ops maintains and reviews this playbook quarterly and after every emergency use (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Recruiters must keep the emergency vendor list updated and check vendor SLAs monthly.

Appendix: rapid interviewer cheat-sheet (one-pager to paste into calendar invites)
- Goal: determine immediate fit, ramp ability, and red flags in 20 minutes
- 0–2m: 30s intro, confirm availability, reason for job change
- 2–8m: targeted resume probe: 2 examples of similar work
- 8–15m: one real-world problem prompt (role specific) — ask for decomposition and next steps
- 15–18m: logistics (start date, OOO windows, visa)
- 18–20m: candidate questions + close

Templates & artifacts location:
- Canonical templates (offer/SOW/one-pager) -> see linked_artifacts entries at top.
- Emergency vendor list: People Ops shared sheet (access via #people-ops pinned links).

Open questions / improvements to track:
- Thresholds: should SLA be 8 hours for some teams? Keep as a variable per team.
- Faster checks for security: can we pre-clear a pool of contractors?
- Measure quality by 30-day retention for emergency hires.

Notes to reviewers:
This is a pragmatic, minimally bureaucratic approach to reduce time-to-hire during critical interruptions while preserving controls (budget, security, and quality checks). Looking for feedback from Eng Leads on acceptable SLA and from Security on interim-access policies.
